case_prompt: An 80-year-old man with a 13-year history of immunoglobulin G kappa smoldering myeloma presented with a 2-year history of dusky, erythematous, indurated patches on the lower abdomen and back and a hyperpigmented plaque on the right upper calf. Six years earlier, he had similar lesions initially diagnosed as tumid lupus that partially improved with topical corticosteroids and fully resolved after 9 months of lenalidomide therapy. On examination, indurated dusky patches were noted on the trunk and a firm hyperpigmented plaque on the calf. A biopsy of the right calf showed dermal sclerosis with hyalinized collagen bundles extending into the subcutis and absence of CD34+ dermal dendrocytes in sclerotic zones. A biopsy of the back revealed dermal sclerosis with abundant interstitial mucin confirmed by colloidal iron stain and diminished CD34+ dendrocytes in the sclerotic zone. Laboratory studies confirmed persistent IgG kappa monoclonal gammopathy; all other tests were normal. Whole-body CT showed no evidence of systemic mucinosis. At that time, a morphea/lupus erythematosus overlap syndrome and mixed connective tissue disease were considered in the histopathologic differential diagnosis.

selection.screen_reason: Morphea-like sclerosis on biopsy in a man with IgG kappa gammopathy whose earlier lesions cleared on lenalidomide supports a paraneoplastic morphea.
